target_claim: The solution claims S◦ can be written explicitly as {y : y^T a_i <= b_i for all i with b_i > 0} intersected with {y = lambda a_i, lambda >= 0 for i with b_i = 0}; this explicit membership predicate is directly implementable and is false.
source_quote: S◦= {y ∈Rn | yTai ≤bi for all i with bi > 0}∩{y ∈Rn | y = λai, λ ≥0 for all i with bi = 0}.
test_sketch: Implement the line-0047 formula as a membership predicate on (A,b,y) with small integer data. Family: n=1, A=[[1]], b=[1], so S=(-inf,1]. Claimed predicate accepts y=-5 since (-5)*1<=1. Brute-force oracle: sample x on an integer grid in S (e.g., x in {-12..1}); at x=-12, y*x=60>1, so y=-5 is not in the true polar ([0,1]). Predicate disagrees with oracle -> claim refuted. Also refutes the intermediate claim (lines 0033-0040) that max{y^T x : a_i^T x <= b_i} = y^T a_i / b_i, which fails for any y not parallel to a_i (e.g., n=2, a=(1,0), b=1, y=(0,1): sup is +inf, formula gives 0).
